title: Cipher and Will
premise: Dominic Joubert has spent twelve years as the town of Marrow Creek's quiet keeper of secrets, filing away the town's sins in probate documents and unspoken agreements. When a will surfaces naming a man who died a decade ago—and a body appears dressed in clothes lifted from Dominic's own closet—they realize someone is weaponizing their own meticulous records against them. As Sheriff's Deputy Ilsa Reyes investigates, Dominic must decide whether to protect the town's buried complicity or finally expose it. The killer is revealed to be the 'dead' man's daughter, who has spent years reconstructing the conspiracy that abandoned her father, and the climax comes at the anniversary dinner where she plans to make the whole town drink to its own guilt. Dominic chooses justice over discretion, testifying to what they've hidden, and finds in Ilsa and the victim's scattered survivors the found family they never let themselves want.
about_author: Wren Kavanagh is the pen name of a former paralegal who spent nine years in small-town estate law before trading case files for fiction. They write mysteries about people who mistake silence for safety.

chapters.title: The Will That Wasn't
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. While closing out an ordinary estate, Dominic discovers a notarized will dated three days after its signer's funeral—signed by Edmund Voss, dead ten years. The document names no heirs, only 'the truth, itemized.' Dominic's instinct is to file it away; instead they lock it in a drawer and lie awake listening to the house settle. Emotional beat: dread disguised as professional calm.

chapters.title: A Body in Borrowed Clothes
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. A stranger is found dead on the courthouse steps wearing Dominic's own missing overcoat and scarf, pockets stuffed with photocopied pages from old case files—pages only Dominic should have access to. Deputy Ilsa Reyes arrives, sharp-eyed and unimpressed by Dominic's composure. Emotional beat: exposure; the invisibility Dominic cultivated begins cracking.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Alphabetized Sins
chapters.summary: POV Dominic, with flashback texture. We learn how Dominic came to Marrow Creek after a scandal ended their city career, and how the town traded silence for services: everyone's secrets live in Dominic's files. Now someone is pulling those files like threads. Emotional beat: complicity examined; Dominic realizes they built the killer's map.

chapters.title: The Deputy Who Doesn't Look Away
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. Ilsa interviews Dominic and notices the lawyer answers questions no one asked. She pulls the victim's identity: a drifter named Callum Bright, recently employed at the Voss orchard. Her captain wants the case closed as robbery; she doesn't believe it. Emotional beat: Ilsa's stubborn integrity sets her against the town's comfortable lies.

chapters.title: What Edmund Voss Grew
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. At the decaying Voss orchard, Dominic learns Edmund died in a fire ruled accidental—the same week he'd threatened to report contaminated groundwater that sickened half the town's children. The anniversary dinner celebrating the orchard's founders is six weeks away. Emotional beat: grief surfacing through anger.

chapters.title: Pages Missing From the Record
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. Ilsa audits the courthouse archives and finds twelve years of documents subtly altered—dates shifted, names struck—in ways requiring legal precision. Every alteration traces back to filings Dominic handled. She confronts Dominic privately, off the record. Emotional beat: wary alliance forming between two people who distrust everyone else.

chapters.title: The Second Letter
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. A letter arrives at Dominic's office, typed, quoting back their own confidential correspondence verbatim: 'You kept the file. Now read it.' Attached is a page listing five names—the men who signed off on the water report. One of them, Councilman Harlan Pike, dies that night. Emotional beat: terror sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: Harlan Pike's Good Name
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. Pike's death is staged as a heart attack, but Ilsa finds his medication swapped—a swap documented in a pharmacy log that was supposedly destroyed years ago. The killer isn't just killing; they're reassembling evidence the town buried. Emotional beat: Ilsa realizes she's investigating a ghost who knows the system better than she does.

chapters.title: The Daughter Nobody Claimed
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Dominic digs into Edmund Voss's estate and finds a daughter, Maren, surrendered to state care after his death—her existence erased from every local record, including ones Dominic filed. Guilt lands hard: Dominic's tidy paperwork helped make her invisible. Emotional beat: shame becoming resolve.

chapters.title: Anniversary Preparations
chapters.summary: POV ensemble (Ilsa primary). The town throws itself into planning the Founders' Anniversary Dinner, willfully festive while two deaths hang unexplained. Mayor Odette Crane pressures Ilsa to close the case before the event. Meanwhile Dominic notices the guest list includes all five names from the letter. Emotional beat: dramatic irony tightening like a wire.

chapters.title: Maren
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Dominic tracks Maren Voss to a neighboring county—she works as a legal archivist, which explains everything about the forged will and altered files. But when Dominic confronts her, she denies killing anyone and shows them her own investigation: proof the fire that killed her father was set. Emotional beat: recognition; two keepers of records seeing themselves in each other.

chapters.title: Someone Is Wearing Maren's Story
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. Ballistics and timeline work clear Maren for both deaths—but the third name on the list, banker Aldous Wrenn, is found alive but terrorized, his office ransacked with documents laid out like an exhibit. Someone else is executing Maren's plan, or steering it. Emotional beat: the mystery deepens; the hunter has a handler.

chapters.title: Odette's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Dominic remembers a sealed trust they drafted years ago for Mayor Crane—funded suspiciously the same month the water report vanished. Confronting Odette quietly, Dominic gets a partial confession: she buried the report to save the orchard's sale, believing she was saving the town. Emotional beat: the banality of the town's sin.

chapters.title: The Fourth Name Crosses Out His Own
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. The fourth conspirator, Dr. Emory Salt, confesses publicly at a council meeting, breaking ranks—then is found dead hours later, an apparent suicide with a note written in his own hand that Ilsa proves was dictated under duress. The killer is always one step ahead because they're reading the investigation itself. Emotional beat: paranoia; nowhere is safe, including the station.

chapters.title: The Leak in the Room
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. Ilsa narrows the leak to someone with access to both her case notes and Dominic's files: her own partner, Sergeant Dale Pruitt, whose family farm took hush money from the orchard sale. She says nothing, plays along, and warns Dominic in ciphered language. Emotional beat: loneliness of integrity; trust becomes tactical.

chapters.title: What Dominic Buried
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. The killer contacts Dominic directly: bring the original water report—the true copy Dominic hid twelve years ago—to the anniversary dinner, or Ilsa becomes the next exhibit. Dominic must reckon with the fact that they've been the final lock on this secret all along. Emotional beat: the cost of neutrality comes due.

chapters.title: Two Keepers, One Plan
chapters.summary: POV alternating Dominic/Ilsa. Dominic and Ilsa finally pool everything: the forged will, Maren's arson evidence, Pruitt's betrayal, Odette's ledger. They decide not to stop the dinner but to use it—the killer wants an audience, so they'll give her one, with the real evidence ready and arrests planned mid-toast. Emotional beat: found-family solidarity; two loners choosing each other's backs.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Under crystal chandeliers, the mayor raises the first toast. Dominic stands, produces the water report, and reads the children's names aloud—the sickened, some dead. The room fractures. In the chaos, the killer moves toward the podium dressed, once again, in clothes taken from someone else's closet: this time, Edmund Voss's restored suit. Emotional beat: catharsis and terror braided together.

chapters.title: The Face Under the Hat
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. The killer is revealed: Ruth Ann Delacroix, the court clerk who processed every file Dominic ever touched—Maren's foster sister, who adopted her mission after Maren gave up. She holds the room at bay with the truth rather than a weapon, daring the town to arrest the messenger. Ilsa talks her down by promising the one thing the town never offered: a real trial. Emotional beat: tragedy without easy villainy.

chapters.title: Arrests and Aftermath
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. Pruitt is arrested for obstruction and evidence tampering; Odette resigns under threat of prosecution; the remaining conspirator turns state's witness. Ruth Ann is charged, but her evidence forces the state to reopen the Voss fire as homicide. Maren watches the courthouse doors open for the first time in her life. Emotional beat: justice arriving imperfectly, but arriving.

chapters.title: Reading the Real Will
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. The forged will is void, but Dominic drafts a genuine memorial instrument at Maren's request, restoring Edmund Voss's name to the land and endowing a fund for the water-sickened families. Dominic burns nothing this time—every secret goes into the open record. Emotional beat: redemption through transparency; the archivist finally archives the truth.

chapters.title: Visible
chapters.summary: POV Dominic, coda. Months later, Dominic keeps the law office but no longer keeps the town's secrets; people come to the door for honest reasons now. Ilsa stays for dinner, arguing amiably about cold cases. Dominic, who chose invisibility for twelve years, lets themselves be known. Final beat: belonging, chosen at last, in a town learning to deserve it.
